name: Wizard Frontend Boilerplate Pro
description: Scaffold production-ready frontend apps with Next.js, React, Vue, Nuxt, or SvelteKit — 28 UI components, OKLCH color palettes, light/dark theming, WCAG AA contrast.
long_description:
A seven-phase scaffolding skill that takes you from zero to a fully themed, component-showcased frontend app in one session.

**Frameworks supported:** Next.js 15 (App Router), React + Vite, Vue 3.5+, Nuxt 4, SvelteKit (Svelte 5)

**What you get out of the box:**
- 28 UI components across 6 categories (Inputs, Display, Feedback, Navigation, Overlay, Data Viz)
- Sidebar showcase with live rendered examples and collapsible code snippets per component
- OKLCH color palette generator — 8 built-in presets or custom hex/OKLCH input
- Three-layer CSS variable token system (palette → semantic → component)
- Light and dark mode with FOUC-prevention inline script and localStorage persistence
- Tailwind v4 (@theme directive) with v3 fallback when needed
- WCAG AA contrast validation baked into the palette generation pipeline
- TypeScript or JavaScript, any of four package managers (pnpm / yarn / npm / bun)

**Optional pairing:** install alongside `ui-ux-pro-max` for higher-fidelity component output. Falls back to built-in Tailwind implementations when the sibling skill is not present.

**Portability:** plain CommonMark only — no agent-specific syntax. All actions are shell commands or file writes, compatible with any agent that supports bash and file I/O.
features: Next.js, React + Vite, Vue 3, Nuxt 4, SvelteKit support
28 UI components with collapsible code snippet showcase
OKLCH palette generator — 8 presets + custom hex/OKLCH input
Optional ui-ux-pro-max integration with standalone fallback
compatibility_notes: Works with any AI agent CLI that can read markdown, execute shell commands, and write files. Uses bash and Python 3 stdlib only — no pip installs required. Pairs best with ui-ux-pro-max skill for enhanced component output.
